newsitem.title: USA: Metal Recovery plant still below capacity.
newsitem.headline: Metal Recovery plant still below capacity.

text.p: Metal Recovery Technologies Inc's galvanized steel scrap recycling plant in East Chicago, Indiana is still operating at below capacity and needs a $2 million injection to work flat out, the company said.
The plant claims to be the world's first commercial zinc recycler, removing zinc from galvanized steel scrap.

"We have been approached by a major international industrial group which may result in a direct investment or joint venture at the East Chicago facility and future plants," Metal Recovery's new Production Senior Vice President, Leon Lohman said.
"Unsatisfactory operational performance has been primarily the result of equipment incompatible with the harsh dezincing environment," Lohman said.
The plant would be profitable once it operates at 40 percent of capacity or 4,000 tons per month of processed scrap.
A $2 million investment would enable to plant to operate flat out at 9,600 tons of scrap steel processed a month, and 240 tons of zinc recovered.

The capital investment plan for 1997 will be raised, but any cash requirements in excess of existing loan facilities will be met in part by Department of Energy grant, and the balance by conventional loan arrangements.
